newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia markets shift focus from Iraq to U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Asia markets shift focus from Iraq to U.S. data.

text.p: Worries about the U.S.-Iraq crisis faded on Asian markets on Thursday, only to be replaced on some bourses by concerns over U.S. jobs figures due out on Friday and domestic issues.
Tokyo stocks climbed cautiously on buying by public funds while Hong Kong and Jakarta dropped on jitters over U.S. employment data and interest rates.
Thai stocks, meanwhile, fell sharply on rumours that some brokerages were hit by client defaults on margin loans. Other Asian markets were generally mixed.
The shock of the U.S. missile attacks on Iraq -- a jolt on Wednesday -- was by Thursday just a faint memory for Japanese investors.
Tokyo stocks gained ground by the end of the session, encouraged by a wide range of buying from public funds. Still, institutional investors remained cautious, limiting further gains, brokers said.
The key 225-issue Nikkei average closed up 177.95 points or 0.88 percent at 20,379.82.
Hong Kong stocks ended weak, with fears about higher interest rates keeping investors cautious and prompting some selling in rate-sensitive areas, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index fell 36.44 points or 0.33 percent to 11,040.51.
Analysts said investors were nervously awaiting Friday's U.S. jobs report.
"People are not sticking their necks out ahead of the numbers in the States in case they signal an increase in interest rates," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage.
Jakarta share prices ended lower on similar worries about the U.S. data, as many operators continued to sell off their stocks in late trade, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.97 points, or 0.54 percent, to 543.03 points.

Taiwan share prices, meanwhile, began to rebound from a recent downturn to finish higher as investors shrugged off worries over the Iraq military conflict. The weighted index ended up 76.18 points or 1.22 percent at 6,304.96.

In the day's biggest drop for Asia, Thai stocks ended down 2.58 percent in moderate trade after investors sold stocks heavily in the afternoon on rumours that some brokerages were hit by client defaults on margin loans, brokers said.
The SET index fell for the sixth straight trading day, dropping 27.06 points to 1,022.68.
The Manila stock exchange remained dull, with prices little changed. The index ended down 6.04 points or 0.19 percent at 3,191.56.
Traders were watching how U.S. markets were reacting to Fed jitters, said Patrick Garcia of L.M. Garcia and Associates. There are fears U.S. rates may be raised when the Fed meets on September 24.
In Seoul, stocks closed lower after volatile trading as fears of another "oil shock" dampened sentiment. The composite stock index closed 4.50 points or 0.57 percent lower at a provisional 787.14.
Australian and New Zealand markets were mixed. The Australian All Ordinaries index ended 1.1 points or 0.05 percent lower at 2,257.4. The NZSE-40 closed 1.80 points or 0.08 percent lower at 2,235.93.
Follow-through buying from Wednesday's recovery nudged up Kuala Lumpur stocks for a second day, but few compelling investing themes emerged to spark excitement, dealers said.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index ended up 2.07 points or 0.19 percent to 1,107.49.
Singapore shares ended higher, rising 15.86 points or 0.76 percent to 2,110.34 on selective blue-chips.
In Singapore, SIMEX Brent futures closed lower from their previous IPE settlement. Brokers said the market remained driven by news coming out from the Gulf rather than by technicals.
October closed at $21.93 a barrel, down 18 cents from its last close on London's IPE with 76 lots traded.

In Tokyo, the dollar moved steadily against the yen and mark, with the market unmoved by German economic growth data that came at the higher end of the forecast range. At 1045 GMT, the dollar was trading at 108.98/9.08 yen and 1.4814/19 marks.
Hong Kong gold closed slightly higher on light European buying, gold traders said. Bullion ended at US$385.90/386.40 an ounce against New York's US$385.50/386.00 close on Wednesday.
